title: Build D87/D88 backtest with fixtures made in temp dirs, no JSON files
summary: Redo job 20261014-002531-pazf's read-only backtest (typed D87/D88 header, supersession parsing, records/ reader, exact-match signal, one introspection record for the earliest D87 event), as in section 5 of the decision-sets review. The tests write their fixture records into a temporary directory at run time, so no JSON fixtures are committed and the policy test every_tracked_file_is_rust_or_a_listed_kind passes.

defaults_applied.how: All new code and fixtures are Rust.
New module has passing tests, with clippy clean.
The fixtures move out of tracked files so the policy test is not weakened.
One focused change that rebuilds the same backtest.
Fixture records contain no personal data or secrets.
Full cargo test, clippy and fmt --check are run.

assumptions: The repository holds none of the earlier job's work (grep for 'backtest' finds only two design docs), so this is a full rebuild with the one fixture change.
The backtest lives in athena-cli, going by the fixture path in the failure output.
Using std::env::temp_dir with a unique subdirectory, or an existing dev-dependency such as tempfile if the workspace already has one, is acceptable (buy-first).
Real records/ are not available to tests, so the tests verify pass and fail logic on synthetic records.

acceptance_criteria.text: No JSON or other non-Rust fixture files are added under crates/athena-cli/tests/fixtures/ or elsewhere; git status shows only Rust, docs and manifest changes.
Backtest tests build their records/ fixtures (jobs outcomes, interventions) in a temporary directory created inside the test, and remove it afterwards.

The backtest reads records/ in Athena code (not through an agent), parses the supersession phrases of docs/decisions.md, defines the typed header for D87 and D88 only, runs one exact-match signal, and emits one introspection record for the earliest matching event naming D87.
The code reports pass or fail by the review's section 5 conditions, and a fail is reported as a finding with its reason, not forced to pass.
Run `cargo test --locked`: all tests pass, including xtask's policy test every_tracked_file_is_rust_or_a_listed_kind and the new backtest tests.
Run `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked` and `cargo fmt --check`: both clean.
No Jev, no brief change, and no governance file is modified.

out_of_scope: Weakening or extending the every_tracked_file_is_rust_or_a_listed_kind policy list
Typed headers for decisions other than D87 and D88
departures: Slightly higher cost than the reference: the rebuild is larger than a typical change because the earlier work is not in the repository.
